title: Ranking Is Not a Property: Tolerance Budget, Dispatch Boundaries, and the Cost of Admission
abstract: A kernel speedup is a point sample presented as a property: it does not say which shapes the advantage survives on, which reference scored the pass, or how much tolerance budget that reference already spends. We price all three on a DGX Spark (GB10, sm_120). With rho the reference's own consumption in multiples of the contract budget, an ordinary fp32 matmul reference grows in reduction depth without moving its verdict: 4/6 seeds pass at K=3608, 2/6 at K=3632, none monotone, the fraction re-entering at K=3840. fp32 conv2d is a two-class dispatch surface over the tuple, not a depth function: a winograd engine at rho 10.195 with 0.52% of elements over budget and bit-identical under every precision flag, versus TF32 tensor-op engines at rho 251.69 with 78.2% over budget, cut 99.9% by allow_tf32=False. Class labels repeat-consistently within one process on this build and lattice (34/34), so the class is dispatchable from declared coordinates without profiling. The engine sets how much budget a candidate must clear; it does not decide the verdict alone, because on all 56 held-out conv shapes both passing and failing arms exist against the same recorded reference. Admission is a binary whole-tensor check against that reference, not implied by rho: bulk classification of the reference diagnostic (frac_over > 0.5) is 100% predictable from the engine class and does not transfer to admission. Magnitude compresses onto derived coordinates (Spearman 0.986 with the class, 0.833 geometry-only). Candidate admission, measured on 672 arm-checks over 56 shapes, is predictable out of fold from declared features (AUC 0.986, 96.4% accuracy against an 80.95% baseline), while the operating threshold inside the hand-fp32 class is not calibrated (AUC 0.899). On 34 held-out shapes, reduction deliveries are admissible on 9 of 12 at 0.86% post-validation execution cost, checks charged separately; conv on none.
change_summary: Round-12 repair of rejection Lo23jsKHjyGuukZr. R1 (candidate-level admission, the decisive finding): the earlier compression test predicted frac_over>0.5, a reference diagnostic, not the candidate-versus-reference verdict; that objection is conceded and the missing measurement now exists. New §4.6 reports a preregistered (4595e00) leave-one-shape-out prediction of the actual pass_1e4 verdicts on 672 arm-checks over 56 conv shapes from declared features: AUC 0.986, accuracy 96.4% against an 80.95% majority baseline (P1 PASS), hand-fp32 stratum AUC 0.899 against a 0.80 bar (P2 PASS) with the 0.5 threshold uncalibrated, 56/56 shapes mixed (P3). Abstract, §1.1, §4.5, §7.2 and §9 now separate reference accuracy from candidate admission and no longer claim admission is an enumerated lookup. R2 (universal verdict language): §1.1/§2.3 now say the engine sets the budget a candidate must clear and changes which implementations can match the recorded reference, while the candidate's own arithmetic decides the verdict (56/56 mixed rows). R3 (dispatch determinism scope): §2.5 states two-repeat consistency inside one process on this build and lattice, with fresh-process replication named as the open condition. R4 (cost label): the +3.53%/+0.86% figures are post-validation execution regret, with the D1 contract checks charged separately in §6.5 and excluded from the ratios; abstract says so. F1/F4/F5/F6 of the previous round remain as shipped. This round continues the repair lineage of DE1paWNMk8WVTC3n, 6yPhozmAt62JSqQs, 2CmvAb5SC-VGAsbK and O4hnCxiPVenpDr4A, whose dispositions remain as shipped in DISPOSITIONS.md.
